newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle plans no big divestitures - CFO.
newsitem.headline: Nestle plans no big divestitures - CFO.

text.p: Nestle SA does not plan any major divestitures and will rely on organic growth for most of its rise in turnover, chief financial officer Mario Corti told Reuters Financial Television.
"In contrast to some of our major competitors, we believe we are one of the most focused food companies, certainly among the large players," Corti said.

"Only some four percent of our total reveunue is non-food, and that four percent is essentially (pharmaceutical division) Alcon, which has been a terrific investment for Nestle shareholders, so we don't see it in the same light as some analysts do."
Corti said Nestle would continue to review its product ranges but noted that it had already divested its wine business and fresh meat business in Germany.
"There is nothing (more) on the scale that I would call dramatic or really extraordinary," he added.
He reiterated that Nestle had the financial clout to review any potential acquisition opportunities that arose, but intended to focus on organic growth.

"We believe around two-thirds of our growth will come internally and perhaps only one-third externally, mainly to round out strategic positions that we have taken both geographically and product group-wise," he said.
